2 Methods summary

2.1 Cohort

Index admissions are any-listed type 2 myocardial infarction (ICD-10-CM I21.A1) among adults, discharged 2018–2022. I21.A1 is overwhelmingly a secondary diagnosis, which is the clinically correct picture for a supply–demand infarction, so the any-listed definition is mandatory; a principal-diagnosis-only cohort is sensitivity S5. The window starts in 2018 because I21.A1 became effective on 1 October 2017; 2016 has no I21.A1 records and 2017 has one quarter, which would manufacture a spurious trend. Project 1 reads only the 2018–2022 files and asserts that no other year is present.

Excluded: records also carrying I21.A9 (other MI type) and records carrying both a type 1 and a type 2 code (uninterpretable as to which event drove the admission; 28,316 such records, reported as a finding in its own right).

Type 1 versus type 2 comparison (secondary aim 2) — descriptive and explicitly NON-CAUSAL. The type 1 comparator (any-listed I21.0–I21.4, I21.9 or I22.x without I21.A1, same years and exclusions, linked for 30-day readmission in the same pass) is used only to describe how the two coded populations differ. The two are not competing treatments, and no causal contrast is estimated or implied.

2.2 Exposure: the precipitant hierarchy

Eight mutually exclusive and exhaustive classes, assigned by a hierarchy frozen before any result was seen (SAP B3.2): (1) sepsis or severe infection; (2) acute GI bleed or blood-loss anaemia; (3) hypertensive emergency; (4) tachyarrhythmia; (5) acute respiratory failure; (6) hypovolaemia or non-cardiogenic shock; (7) perioperative; (8) none of the above. Ranks 1–6 are tested on the principal diagnosis first, then on any secondary diagnosis; rank 7 is procedure-based; rank 8 is the residual. The SAP asked for present-on-admission-positive secondary diagnoses; no NRD file carries a POA indicator, so all secondary diagnoses are used and a complication that arose after admission cannot be distinguished from a precipitant (a stated limitation). Reference class: Sepsis or severe infection.

ImportantDefinitional decisions a cardiologist reviewer will check

Cardiogenic shock (R57.0) is not a precipitant. It is a consequence of the infarction and is entered as a covariate.

Hypertensive emergency is I16.1 and I16.9 only. I16.0 is hypertensive urgency and is never a precipitant in any rank (including rank 7, which is procedure-based); 39,889 index admissions carry I16.0 and are reported only as a count.

Perioperative = an ICD-10-PCS Section 0 (Medical and Surgical) procedure with approach 0 (open) or 4 (percutaneous endoscopic). Neither the NRD nor the AHRQ PRCCSR file carries an operating-room flag. The received rule also admitted natural-opening approaches (7/8/F), which capture bedside urinary catheters, feeding tubes, intubation and diagnostic endoscopy; under that rule 22,674 admissions would be perioperative versus 11,533 under the rule used (Table S0b).

The raw co-occurrence of the classes before the hierarchy is Table S1b.

2.3 Outcome, design and estimation

Thirty-day all-cause readmission, linked within calendar year; December discharges, in-hospital deaths and transfers out are excluded from the index cohort. Design-based throughout: DISCWT weights, year-unique strata and clusters integer-coded, the design built once on the full cohort and every analysis a subset() of it; singleton strata centred. Primary model: survey-weighted logistic regression with age as a restricted cubic spline; the precipitant block is tested jointly first, then seven pairwise contrasts versus sepsis. Adjusted absolute risks by g-computation with delta-method intervals; overlap weighting (ATO), applied pairwise, is the co-estimator. Costs in 2022 US dollars using CPI-U, All Items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted, annual average (CUUR0000SA0). Nothing representing 1–10 unweighted discharges is reported, and complementary suppression prevents recovery by subtraction (Section 16).

The following declared factor levels had no observations in the analytic cohort and were dropped before modelling, so that they could not appear as silent NA coefficients: Hospital bed size: Missing/other; Hospital location and teaching status: Missing/other; Hospital ownership: Missing/other. No reference category was affected.

The Nationwide Readmissions Database contains de-identified, publicly available administrative data and this analysis was therefore determined to be non-human-subjects research and exempt from institutional review board review. The HCUP Data Use Agreement was executed before any data were accessed.

Weighted percentages are design-based national estimates using the HCUP discharge weight; unweighted n is the actual NRD sample size. Continuous variables are reported as design-weighted mean (SD). Standardized mean differences are reported in place of p-values because with 870,486 observations every p-value would be <0.001 and would convey nothing about the magnitude of an imbalance. Because the exposure has eight levels there is no single standardized mean difference; the figure shown is the MAXIMUM absolute standardized mean difference across the seven pairwise comparisons against the reference class (sepsis or severe infection), and for a categorical variable it is the maximum across that variable’s levels as well. 42 of 46 characteristics show |SMD| >= 0.10: Age, years, mean (SD); Age group, % (unweighted n); Sex, % (unweighted n); Median household income quartile (patient ZIP code), % (unweighted n); Patient residence (NCHS urban-rural classification), % (unweighted n); Admission day, % (unweighted n); Admission type, % (unweighted n); Hospital bed size, % (unweighted n); Hospital location and teaching status, % (unweighted n); Hospital ownership, % (unweighted n); Type 2 MI coded as the principal diagnosis, % (unweighted n); Cardiogenic shock at index, % (unweighted n); Invasive mechanical ventilation at index, % (unweighted n); Chronic kidney disease stage, % (unweighted n); Dialysis dependence at index, % (unweighted n); Known coronary artery disease (I25.1x/I25.7x), % (unweighted n); Prior revascularization (Z95.1/Z95.5), % (unweighted n); Atrial fibrillation or flutter (I48), % (unweighted n); COVID-19 at index (U07.1), % (unweighted n); Elixhauser comorbidity count, mean (SD); Congestive heart failure, % (unweighted n); Valvular disease, % (unweighted n); Pulmonary circulation disorders, % (unweighted n); Peripheral vascular disorders, % (unweighted n); Hypertension, uncomplicated, % (unweighted n); Hypertension, complicated, % (unweighted n); Other neurological disorders, % (unweighted n); Chronic pulmonary disease, % (unweighted n); Diabetes, uncomplicated, % (unweighted n); Liver disease, % (unweighted n); Obesity, % (unweighted n); Weight loss, % (unweighted n); Coagulopathy, % (unweighted n); Metastatic cancer, % (unweighted n); Solid tumour without metastasis, % (unweighted n); Depression, % (unweighted n); Alcohol abuse, % (unweighted n); Drug abuse, % (unweighted n); Cardiac arrhythmias (excluded from the model by pre-specification), % (unweighted n); Fluid and electrolyte disorders (excluded from the model by pre-specification), % (unweighted n); Renal failure (excluded from the model by pre-specification), % (unweighted n); Blood loss anaemia (excluded from the model by pre-specification), % (unweighted n). The eight precipitant classes are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by construction and sum to the analytic cohort. The Elixhauser cardiac-arrhythmia, fluid-and-electrolyte, renal-failure and anaemia flags are shown here but were removed from every model by pre-specification, because each overlaps a precipitant class by construction; showing them lets the reader verify that argument rather than take it on trust. Any cell representing fewer than 11 unweighted discharges is suppressed in accordance with the HCUP Data Use Agreement.

Each off-diagonal cell is the number of admissions carrying both the row class and the column class, with the percentage taken over the row class. This table is published because it is the direct evidence for why a hierarchy is necessary at all: these conditions co-occur constantly, and any assignment rule must resolve that overlap. The hierarchy used is stated in full in the Methods and was frozen before any result was seen. Cells below 11 unweighted discharges are suppressed.

All percentages are design-based national estimates with 95% confidence intervals from the survey design; the bracketed figure is the unweighted event count. Readmission, length of stay, cost and disposition are computed on the analytic cohort (discharge survivors with a complete 30-day window and a complete covariate vector). In-hospital mortality is computed on the larger denominator that RETAINS in-hospital deaths, because that is the only population on which a mortality rate is interpretable; the two denominators are reported separately and are never mixed. Readmission characteristics are computed on index admissions that were followed by a readmission and are therefore conditional on being readmitted. Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention and bypass grafting are reported as PROCESS MEASURES describing how coded type 2 myocardial infarction was managed; they are not outcomes and are not modelled as such. These are unadjusted comparisons; the adjusted estimates are in Table 3.

The primary model is a survey-weighted logistic regression of 30-day all-cause readmission on the eight-level precipitating illness class, with sepsis or severe infection as the reference, adjusted for the pre-specified covariate blocks: age modelled as a restricted cubic spline with four knots, sex, primary payer, ZIP-code income quartile, NCHS urban-rural residence, weekend admission, admission type, hospital bed size, location and teaching status, ownership, discharge year, the Elixhauser comorbidity set with the pre-specified exclusions below, cardiogenic shock, mechanical ventilation, chronic kidney disease stage, known coronary artery disease, prior revascularization and whether the index admission included coronary angiography. Design-based joint Wald test across the whole eight-level precipitant block: F(7, 8855) = 92.44, p <0.001. Adjusted absolute risks were obtained by marginal standardization over the whole analytic cohort with delta-method variance on the design-based covariance matrix and t critical values on 8928 design degrees of freedom. FIVE ELIXHAUSER FLAGS WERE REMOVED FROM EVERY MODEL BY PRE-SPECIFICATION, not after inspection, because each overlaps a precipitant class by construction and adjusting for it would attenuate the very contrast being estimated: Blood loss anaemia (excluded from the model by pre-specification) (D62 is the rank-2 precipitant itself); Deficiency anaemia (excluded from the model by pre-specification) (same clinical entity as the rank-2 precipitant); Cardiac arrhythmias (excluded from the model by pre-specification) (I47/I48/I49 is the rank-4 precipitant itself); Fluid and electrolyte disorders (excluded from the model by pre-specification) (E86/E87 is the rank-6 precipitant itself); Renal failure (excluded from the model by pre-specification) (superseded in finer detail by the CKD_Stage covariate). Chronic pulmonary disease was deliberately RETAINED, because chronic disease is a confounder while acute respiratory failure is the exposure, and ICD-10-CM distinguishes them. Atrial fibrillation and the Elixhauser comorbidity count are reported in Table 1 but are not covariates: the former is definitionally the tachyarrhythmia class, the latter is a linear combination of flags already entered individually. No pre-specified covariate required removal by the sparse-cell guard. The Model 4 to Model 5 change is attenuation consistent with mediation and is not an adjusted estimate.

E-values are reported on the RISK RATIO scale, never on the odds ratio, which would overstate them. Each is the minimum strength of association, on the risk ratio scale, that an unmeasured confounder would need with both the precipitant class and 30-day readmission, above and beyond the measured covariates, to explain the observed contrast away. The most plausible such confounder here is ILLNESS SEVERITY: the NRD carries no vital signs, no laboratory values and no troponin concentration, and a sicker patient is both more likely to receive a given precipitant code and more likely to be readmitted.

A readmission is CONCORDANT when the DXCCSR v2025.1 default category of its principal diagnosis falls in the same clinical domain as the precipitating illness class assigned at the index admission; the full class-to-category mapping was frozen before any result was seen and is reproduced in the supplement. A readmission is CARDIAC when that category is CIR009, CIR010, CIR011, CIR017 or CIR019. The two are not mutually exclusive: a tachyarrhythmia precipitant followed by a dysrhythmia readmission is both. The ‘none of the above’ class has no concordant set by construction and is scored as undefined rather than zero; 36,007 readmissions fall in that class and are excluded from the concordance column only. The third and fourth columns are conditional on being readmitted and answer ‘what did they come back with?’; the fifth column is the absolute risk of a concordant readmission among all index admissions in that class and is the quantity to quote alongside the overall readmission rate. Adjusted for the full primary covariate block, the design-based joint Wald test of whether concordance differs across precipitant classes gives p <0.001. Cells below 11 unweighted readmissions are suppressed under the HCUP Data Use Agreement.

9 Table 7. Type 2 versus type 1 myocardial infarction (descriptive, non-causal)

WarningDescriptive and explicitly NON-CAUSAL

Type 1 and type 2 myocardial infarction are not competing treatments. No patient could have been assigned to one rather than the other, and the ‘effect’ of being coded type 2 is not a quantity that exists. What follows is a case-mix-standardized description of how the two coded populations differ, and it must be described that way in the manuscript.

Quantity Estimate

THIS COMPARISON IS DESCRIPTIVE AND IS NOT CAUSAL. Type 1 and type 2 myocardial infarction are not competing treatments; no patient could have been assigned to one rather than the other, and the ‘effect’ of being coded type 2 rather than type 1 is not a quantity that exists. The adjusted figure below is a case-mix-standardized DESCRIPTION of how the two coded populations differ, reported only because an unadjusted comparison between populations this dissimilar in age and comorbidity would be uninterpretable even descriptively. Standardized to the measured case mix of the combined cohort: adjusted OR 1.04 (1.03–1.05), adjusted risk difference 0.46 (0.33–0.59) percentage points. The precipitant class is deliberately absent from that model because it is undefined for the type 1 arm. Type 1 myocardial infarction was defined as any-listed I21.0-I21.4, I21.9 or I22.x WITHOUT I21.A1; 28,316 records carrying both a type 1 and a type 2 code were excluded from both arms, because such a record is uninterpretable as to which event drove the admission. A further 15,154 records coded I21.A9 (other myocardial infarction type) were excluded rather than pooled. The size of the type 1 / type 2 overlap is a finding in its own right and is worth a sentence in the Results.

ALL SUBGROUP RESULTS ARE EXPLORATORY and are not adjusted for multiplicity. Within each subgroup the primary model was refitted on the primary covariate block, and two quantities are reported: the design-based JOINT Wald test across the whole eight-level precipitant block, which is the substantive question in that subgroup, and the pre-specified headline contrast (Tachyarrhythmia versus Sepsis or severe infection), which is shown so that the direction of the association is visible. Effect modification is assessed by a design-based Wald test on the WHOLE interaction block, fitted on the rows with a non-missing modifier, with the modifier’s deterministic parent covariate removed from that model so that no coefficient is aliased (chronic kidney disease stage for the CKD grouping, discharge year for the pandemic-era grouping). Non-overlapping subgroup confidence intervals are NOT evidence of interaction and are not interpreted as such. Terms that became constant or sparse inside a subgroup were dropped from that fit and are listed in the run log. No subgroup finding appears in the Conclusions.

WarningRead this before quoting any trend number

Three qualifications apply to every trend result reported here and must appear alongside them in the manuscript. First, these are five independent annual cross-sections drawn from a partly changing hospital sample, not a longitudinal cohort; NRD patient linkage does not cross calendar years and hospital identifiers are reset each year. Second, and most importantly for this study, I21.A1 became effective on 1 October 2017 and was still diffusing into routine use across the study window, while high-sensitivity troponin assays were being adopted across US hospitals over the same period and the Fourth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction formalised the type 2 category in 2018. A rise in coded volume therefore reflects ASCERTAINMENT at least as much as incidence, and NO BIOLOGICAL TREND IS CLAIMED. Third, 2020 is anomalous because of pandemic admission avoidance, COVID-19 coding and capacity effects, and is examined in the leave-2020-out sensitivity analysis S2. The trend test enters discharge year as a continuous term replacing the year factor, which is a design-based test; Joinpoint and segmented regression on the annual point estimates are not appropriate because they ignore the survey design. Whether the association between precipitant class and readmission itself changed across the window was tested ONCE, as a single precipitant-by-year interaction (p 0.443), and not as five year-specific sets of estimates.

Sensitivity analyses are consistency checks and are NOT corrected for multiplicity; they are judged on whether the point estimate moves, not on whether a p-value crosses 0.05. Every subset was taken with subset() on the survey design constructed ONCE on the full cohort. Each row reports the design-based joint Wald test across the whole precipitant block together with the pre-specified headline contrast (Tachyarrhythmia versus Sepsis or severe infection); all seven contrasts under every analysis are in Table 9b. S6, the PRESENT-ON-ADMISSION-RESTRICTED precipitant assignment pre-specified in SAP B3.5, is NOT ESTIMABLE: no NRD file in the 2016-2022 series carries a present-on-admission indicator. It is reported as such, and S6b (assignment from the principal diagnosis only) is shown beside it as the closest estimable substitute. The SAP’s study-specific S7 (exclude 2020) is the common leave-2020-out analysis and is reported once, as S2/S7. Overlap weighting is applied PAIRWISE; each estimate is the average treatment effect in the overlap population of that pair, with the propensity score fitted within the pair and the outcome model refitted on the pair’s subset of the full-cohort design re-weighted by the overlap weight. The design-based variance treats the estimated weights as fixed. Estimates derived from any class-by-outcome cell with fewer than 11 unweighted discharges are suppressed. The Cox model in S4 is a sensitivity analysis only, fitted on the full cohort with non-events retained and censored at day 30. The Cox design matrix was of full rank and required no further removals.

13 Model diagnostics

Table S4. Model diagnostics.
Diagnostic Value Interpretation
Maximum variance inflation factor (per design-matrix column) 3.55 Below the pre-specified threshold of 5; no collinearity concern
Maximum VIF among the seven precipitant dummy columns 1.72 Reported separately because the exposure contributes seven dummy columns; an inflated value here would indicate that a covariate still overlaps a precipitant class despite the pre-specified removals
Survey-weighted c-statistic (tie-corrected) 0.622 Reported without a threshold; discrimination is not the objective of an aetiological model
Design-based decile calibration test (survey analogue of Hosmer-Lemeshow) <0.001 With a cohort of this size any calibration test will reject. Figure S3 is the substantive evidence; this p-value is reported for completeness only and is not interpreted alone.
Covariates removed by the sparse-cell guard None Every removal is named here and in the Methods section
Minimum unweighted cell enforced on every reported table 11 HCUP Data Use Agreement

Variance inflation factors are computed per design-matrix column rather than aggregated to a generalized VIF, which is the conservative reading: if no individual dummy column is inflated then no multi-level factor is either. The maximum among the seven precipitant dummy columns is reported separately, because the pre-specified removal of five Elixhauser flags was justified on the grounds that they overlap precipitant classes by construction, and this is the number that shows whether that removal succeeded. The c-statistic is survey-weighted and tie-corrected. The calibration test is the survey analogue of the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and is NOT the Archer-Lemeshow F-adjusted mean residual test; it should not be described as such. Singleton strata were centred at the grand mean (survey.lonely.psu = ‘adjust’) rather than removed; 5 stratum/strata contained a single primary sampling unit. All manually constructed intervals use t critical values on 8,928 design degrees of freedom rather than 1.96.

S6, present-on-admission-restricted precipitant assignment: NOT ESTIMABLE. No NRD file in the 2016-2022 series carries a present-on-admission indicator. It is reported as not estimable in Table 9, and S6b (assignment from the principal diagnosis only) is shown beside it as the closest estimable substitute: a precipitant recorded as the principal diagnosis is necessarily the reason for admission.
